questions.question: What happens on the server when a shopper hits the button to put a product in their basket?

answer.content:
{"answer": "Hitting the button doesn't touch the server directly in the component: `AddToCart` in `components/cart/add-to-cart.tsx` renders `SubmitButton`, which is gated on `availableForSale` and `selectedVariantId` (variant comes from `useSearchParams()`), and dispatches a cart action rather than doing any fetching itself. On the server the request lands in the cart server-actions module, `components/cart/actions.ts`, where `addItem` accepts `selectedVariantId: string | undefined` and is the entry point that actually mutates cart state.

From there the Shopify layer takes over:

- `components/cart/actions.ts` — `addItem` (plus `updateItemQuantity`, `removeItem`, `redirectToCheckout`); `createCartAndSetCookie` calls `createCart()` and persists the new cart by writing the `cartId` cookie, so a first-time shopper gets cart identity here.
- `lib/shopify/index.ts` — `addToCart`/`updateCart`/`removeFromCart` send the Storefront GraphQL mutations through `shopifyFetch`; they read `cartId` from cookies with a non-null assertion, so a missing cookie throws. Responses go through the `reshape*` helpers (`reshapeProduct`/`reshapeProducts`) which drop products tagged `HIDDEN_PRODUCT_TAG` (`lib/constants.ts`).
- `lib/shopify/types.ts` — `Cart`/`Product` are the reshaped contracts returned to the UI; note `CartItem.id` is `string | undefined`.

Not in the evidence: the exact body of `addItem`, the GraphQL cart mutation names, and any `revalidateTag(TAGS.cart)` call — the search returned no symbol-level section for `components/cart/actions.ts` or the cart mutations in `lib/shopify/index.ts`.", "citations": ["component:components-cart-add-to-cart-tsx", "code:components-cart-add-to-cart-tsx:add-to-cart", "code:components-cart-add-to-cart-tsx:submit-button", "component:components-cart-actions-ts", "component:lib-shopify-index-ts", "code:lib-shopify-index-ts:reshape-product", "code:lib-shopify-index-ts:reshape-products", "component:lib-shopify-types-ts", "component:lib-constants-ts", "code:lib-constants-ts:hidden-product-tag", "code:lib-constants-ts:tags"]}

questions.question: When a merchant edits a product in their store admin, how does the website stop showing the stale version?

answer.content:
{"answer":"Stale product data is cleared via Shopify webhook-driven revalidation: when a merchant edits a product, Shopify pings the `revalidate` handler in `lib/shopify/index.ts`, which invalidates the cached render output and always answers 200 so Shopify stops retrying. The product views are server components (`ProductPage` in `app/product/[handle]/page.tsx`, `Carousel`, `ProductDescription`) that fetch on render, so once the cache entry is dropped the next request re-fetches fresh data from the Storefront API and reshapes it via `reshapeProduct`/`reshapeProducts`.

- `component:lib-shopify-index-ts` — `revalidate` is the webhook entry point in `lib/shopify/index.ts`; per its notes it returns 200 even for unmatched topics so Shopify stops retrying.
- `code:lib-constants-ts:tags` (`component:lib-constants-ts`) — `TAGS` fixes the `collections`, `products`, `cart` tag names, which are the cache tags this invalidation keys on; the notes say to keep these strings stable.
- `code:app-product-handle-page-tsx:product-page` / `code:components-product-product-description-tsx:product-description` — the rendering side that re-fetches and shows the updated product after invalidation.
- `code:lib-shopify-index-ts:reshape-product` — where the refreshed GraphQL payload becomes the app `Product` shape.

Note: the evidence only gives the summary of `revalidate` (lines noted but not excerpted), so the exact `revalidateTag`/`revalidatePath` calls and the route file that wires Shopify's webhook to `revalidate` are not shown in these excerpts.","citations":["component:lib-shopify-index-ts","code:lib-constants-ts:tags","component:lib-constants-ts","code:app-product-handle-page-tsx:product-page","code:components-product-product-description-tsx:product-description","code:lib-shopify-index-ts:reshape-product","code:lib-shopify-index-ts:reshape-products","container:vercel-commerce"]}

answer.content:
{"answer": "The evidence shows the item link target but not the file that renders it. `ProductGridItems` in `components/layout/product-grid-items.tsx` links each item to ``/product/${product.handle}``, so the single-item page is the App Router route under `/product/[handle]` — but no product page file (e.g. `app/product/[handle]/page.tsx`) appears in the search results or selected scopes, so I can't name it from this evidence.

What the evidence does cover:
- `components/layout/product-grid-items.tsx` → `ProductGridItems` builds the per-item link (`/product/${product.handle}`) from a Shopify `Product`, using `GridTileImage`.
- `components/grid/tile.tsx` → `GridTileImage` renders the tile image/label shown in those grids.
- `app/search/[collection]/page.tsx` → `CategoryPage` shows the pattern a dynamic route page follows here (await `params`, fetch data, render), which the product page likely mirrors — but that file is for collections, not single items.
- `lib/shopify/types.ts` → `Page`, `ShopifyPageOperation`, `ShopifyPagesOperation` define the single-page data contract (`pageByHandle`, `handle`), used for CMS-style pages rather than products.

questions.question: Where do plain content pages like 'About' or 'Terms' come from — are they written in the repo?

answer.content:
{"answer":"No — plain content pages like "About" or "Terms" are **not written in the repo**. They are CMS pages authored in Shopify and fetched at request time over the Storefront API; the repo only supplies the route shell and the GraphQL queries.

- `app/[page]/page.tsx` (`Page`, `generateMetadata`) takes the URL segment and calls `getPage` to load the page, returning `notFound()` if Shopify has no match — so page existence is decided by Shopify content, not by files in the repo.
- `lib/shopify/index.ts` (`getPage`, `getPages`, `shopifyFetch`) performs the actual fetch and returns the `Page` record (`title`, `seo`, body) straight from the API.
- `lib/shopify/queries/page.ts` (`getPageQuery`, `getPagesQuery`, `pageFragment`) holds the GraphQL that pulls `pageByHandle` / `pages(first: 100)`; `pageFragment` defines which fields (title, seo, body) come back.
- `lib/shopify/types.ts` (`Page`, `ShopifyPageOperation`, `ShopifyPagesOperation`) types that content contract.
- The rendering shell is in-repo only: `app/[page]/layout.tsx` (`Layout`) wraps children plus `Footer`, `components/prose.tsx` (`Prose`) renders the fetched HTML verbatim, and `app/[page]/opengraph-image.tsx` (`Image`) titles the OG image from `page.seo?.title || page.title`.

To change an About/Terms page's text or SEO, edit it in Shopify admin — the only in-repo levers are the query fields in `pageFragment` and the layout/prose presentation.","citations":["component:app-page-page-tsx","code:app-page-page-tsx:page","code:app-page-page-tsx:generate-metadata","component:lib-shopify-index-ts","code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-page","code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-pages","code:lib-shopify-index-ts:shopify-fetch","component:lib-shopify-queries-page-ts","code:lib-shopify-queries-page-ts:get-page-query","code:lib-shopify-queries-page-ts:get-pages-query","code:lib-shopify-queries-page-ts:page-fragment","component:lib-shopify-types-ts","code:lib-shopify-types-ts:page","code:lib-shopify-types-ts:shopify-page-operation","code:lib-shopify-types-ts:shopify-pages-operation","component:app-page-layout-tsx","code:app-page-layout-tsx:layout","component:components-layout-footer-tsx","component:components-prose-tsx","component:app-page-opengraph-image-tsx","code:app-page-opengraph-image-tsx:image"]}

questions.question: What settings do I need to supply to connect this storefront to my own shop?

answer.content:
{"answer":"To point this storefront at your own shop, you supply Shopify environment variables: `SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN` and `SHOPIFY_STOREFRONT_ACCESS_TOKEN`. They're checked at startup and then used to build every Storefront API request.

- `lib/utils.ts` — `validateEnvironmentVariables` (lines 22–51) enumerates the required Shopify variables and fails startup if they're missing.
- `lib/shopify/index.ts` — `shopifyFetch` (lines 71–123) throws if `SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN` is unset (it builds `endpoint`) and sends the token via the `X-Shopify-Storefront-Access-Token` header, with `key` (line 65) holding the access token value.
- The system is a Next.js storefront backed by Shopify's Storefront API (`system:vercel-commerce`, `container:vercel-commerce`), with `lib/shopify/index.ts` as the single data gateway.
- Related but not shop credentials: `lib/utils.ts` `baseUrl` uses `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL` with a localhost fallback.

Note: the evidence shows these two names but not the full checked list inside `validateEnvironmentVariables`, so any additional variables it enforces are not in the evidence.","citations":["system:vercel-commerce","container:vercel-commerce","component:lib-utils-ts","code:lib-utils-ts:validate-environment-variables","component:lib-shopify-index-ts","code:lib-shopify-index-ts:shopify-fetch","code:lib-shopify-index-ts:key"]}

questions.question: Can I run this against a different ecommerce platform instead, and what would I need to replace?

answer.content:
{"answer": "Yes — the app is built so Shopify lives behind one integration layer, so you could target another platform, but you'd rewrite that layer and a handful of hardcoded Shopify assumptions in the UI.

**Replace wholesale:**
- `lib/shopify/index.ts` — `shopifyFetch`, the `reshape*` helpers, `getMenu`, cart mutations, and webhook `revalidate` (`component:lib-shopify-index-ts`, `code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-menu`).
- `lib/shopify/types.ts` — the `Cart`/`Product`/`Collection` and `Shopify*Operation` contract every page renders against (`component:lib-shopify-types-ts`).
- The GraphQL strings: `lib/shopify/queries/menu.ts` (`getMenuQuery`), `lib/shopify/mutations/cart.ts`, `lib/shopify/fragments/cart.ts` (`component:lib-shopify-queries-menu-ts`, `component:lib-shopify-mutations-cart-ts`, `component:lib-shopify-fragments-cart-ts`).
- Env validation in `lib/utils.ts` (`validateEnvironmentVariables` checks `SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN`, `SHOPIFY_STOREFRONT_ACCESS_TOKEN`), used by `app/sitemap.ts` (`component:lib-utils-ts`, `component:app-sitemap-ts`).

**Then fix Shopify-flavoured assumptions:**
- `lib/constants.ts`: `HIDDEN_PRODUCT_TAG` ("nextjs-frontend-hidden") and `TAGS` (`component:lib-constants-ts`).
- `components/layout/navbar/index.tsx` hardcodes menu handle `next-js-frontend-header-menu`; `components/carousel.tsx` hardcodes collection `hidden-homepage-carousel` (`code:components-carousel-tsx:carousel`); `getMenu` rewrites `/collections`→`/search` URLs (`code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-menu`).
- `components/product/variant-selector.tsx` assumes Shopify's option/variant model (`code:components-product-variant-selector-tsx:variant-selector`).
- Cosmetic: `metadata` in `app/page.tsx` mentions Shopify (`code:app-page-tsx:metadata`).

Presentation components (`components/grid/index.tsx`, `components/grid/tile.tsx`, `components/layout/footer-menu.tsx`) are platform-agnostic and can stay. questions.question: Where are the sort choices like 'price low to high' or 'latest arrivals' defined?

answer.content:
{"answer": "The sort choices like "Price: Low to high" and "Latest arrivals" are defined in **`lib/constants.ts`**, in the `sorting` array (`SortFilterItem[]`), with `defaultSort` as its first entry (Relevance, `slug: null`).

- `sorting` (`code:lib-constants-ts:sorting`) lists each option as `{ title, slug, sortKey, reverse }` — e.g. `Latest arrivals` (`latest-desc`, `CREATED_AT`, reverse) and `Price: Low to high` (`price-asc`, `PRICE`).
- The `SortFilterItem` type (`code:lib-constants-ts:sort-filter-item`) constrains `sortKey` to `RELEVANCE | BEST_SELLING | CREATED_AT | PRICE`; `defaultSort` (`code:lib-constants-ts:default-sort`) is the fallback.
- Consumers: `app/search/layout.tsx` renders them via `<FilterList list={sorting} title="Sort by" />` (`code:app-search-layout-tsx:search-layout`), and `app/search/page.tsx` (`code:app-search-page-tsx:search-page`) / `app/search/[collection]/page.tsx` (`code:app-search-collection-page-tsx:category-page`) resolve the `sort` query param against `sorting` and fall back to `defaultSort`.
- The active row UI is `SortFilterItem` in `components/layout/search/filter/item.tsx` (`code:components-layout-search-filter-item-tsx:sort-filter-item`), matching `searchParams.get("sort")` to `item.slug`.
- The chosen `sortKey`/`reverse` flow into Shopify via `getProducts`/`getCollectionProducts` (`code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-products`, `code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-collection-products`), which map `CREATED_AT` → `CREATED` for collections.", "citations": ["component:lib-constants-ts", "code:lib-constants-ts:sorting", "code:lib-constants-ts:sort-filter-item", "code:lib-constants-ts:default-sort", "code:app-search-layout-tsx:search-layout", "code:app-search-page-tsx:search-page", "code:app-search-collection-page-tsx:category-page", "code:components-layout-search-filter-item-tsx:sort-filter-item", "code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-products", "code:lib-shopify-index-ts:get-collection-products"]}

questions.question: When a shopper chooses a size or colour, how does the site work out which exact version of the product gets added?

answer.content:
{"answer":"The chosen size/colour is written into the URL, and `AddToCart` resolves it to a Shopify variant ID before adding anything.

- `components/product/variant-selector.tsx` — `VariantSelector` and `Combination` render the option choices and push the picked option values into the query string (`useSearchParams`/`useRouter`), so the selection lives in the URL rather than component state.
- `components/cart/add-to-cart.tsx` — `AddToCart` reads those query params and finds the variant whose `selectedOptions` all match (`option.value === searchParams.get(option.name.toLowerCase())`); it falls back to `variants[0].id` when the product has only one variant, producing `selectedVariantId`, then looks up `finalVariant` by id.
- `components/cart/add-to-cart.tsx` — `SubmitButton` gates the form on `availableForSale` and `selectedVariantId`.
- `components/cart/actions.ts` — `addItem` receives that `selectedVariantId` as `merchandiseId` and calls `addToCart([{ merchandiseId, quantity: 1 }])`, erroring if no variant was resolved.
- `components/product/product-description.tsx` — `ProductDescription` wires it together: it renders `VariantSelector` with `product.options`/`product.variants` and then `AddToCart`.
- `lib/shopify/fragments/product.ts` — `productFragment` supplies `options { name, values }` and `variants { id, selectedOptions, availableForSale }`, which is what matching depends on.

Product shape (`Product`, `ProductVariant`) comes from `lib/shopify/types.ts` (`Product`).
